papers.title: Integrating heterogeneity into topologically associating domain boundary prediction in large genomic context in human.
papers.abstract: A fundamental understanding of genome organization relies on accurately annotating topologically associating domains (TADs) and their boundaries. This is crucial for understanding how cis-regulatory elements regulate gene expression. To go beyond calling TADs and boundaries from Hi-C data, several machine learning-based methods have been proposed to go the step further and predict TAD boundaries from genomic sequences. As the growing evidence of TADs and their boundaries, TADs have been proved exhibiting diverse properties, such as differences in replication timing and epigenetic patterns. How
papers.summary: This paper presents a new machine learning approach that integrates heterogeneity across cell types and genomic contexts to improve the prediction of topologically associating domain (TAD) boundaries from DNA sequence. By accounting for diverse TAD properties, the method achieves more accurate and generalizable boundary predictions compared to existing tools, offering a better framework for understanding genome organization and gene regulation.

papers.title: LncPNdeep: A long non-coding RNA classifier based on large language model with peptide and nucleotide embedding.
papers.abstract: Accurate classification of long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) is essential for transcriptome annotation and understanding gene regulation. Existing computational methods predominantly rely on nucleotide sequence features, frequently overlooking biologically relevant peptide signals encoded within lncRNAs. To overcome this limitation, we developed LncPNdeep, an integrative deep learning framework that combines nucleotide and peptide embeddings extracted via masked language models, specifically utilizing contextual representations from BigBird, Longformer, and ProtTrans. By fusing both features in a
papers.summary: LncPNdeep is a new deep learning tool that classifies long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) by combining both nucleotide sequence and peptide-level features extracted from large language models, improving accuracy over methods that use only nucleotide sequences. The approach leverages masked language models (BigBird, Longformer, ProtTrans) to capture contextual information from both RNA and protein domains, addressing a gap in existing computational methods.

papers.title: Research priorities in chronic lung allograft dysfunction: A machine learning-assisted bibliometric analysis.
papers.abstract: Chronic lung allograft dysfunction (CLAD), the leading cause of death beyond year one post-transplant, encompasses bronchiolitis obliterans syndrome (BOS), restrictive allograft syndrome (RAS), and mixed allograft syndrome (MAS), formalized by the 2019 ISHLT consensus. How thematic priorities have evolved and whether research effort tracks phenotype burden have not been systematically examined.
papers.summary: This study uses machine learning-assisted bibliometric analysis to map research themes and priorities in chronic lung allograft dysfunction (CLAD), a major cause of late mortality after lung transplantation. It reveals how thematic focus has evolved over time and whether research effort aligns with the burden of different CLAD phenotypes.

papers.title: Identification of IL1RN, MUC1, and SERPINA1 as key NET-related biomarkers in ulcerative colitis-associated intestinal fibrosis via bioinformatics and experimental validation.
papers.abstract: Long-term recurrent episodes of ulcerative colitis (UC) can lead to intestinal fibrosis (IF), which severely affects patient prognosis. Neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) have been identified as critical drivers of various fibrotic diseases; however, their precise role and regulatory mechanisms in UC-associated intestinal fibrosis (UC-IF) remain to be systematically elucidated. Therefore, identifying the key regulatory genes through which NETs participate in UC-IF is highly important for the diagnosis and treatment of this condition.
papers.summary: This study identifies IL1RN, MUC1, and SERPINA1 as key NET-related biomarkers in ulcerative colitis-associated intestinal fibrosis using bioinformatics and experimental validation. These findings may aid in the diagnosis and treatment of this condition.

papers.title: LLM-powered Functional Gene Set Summarization with genesetGPT.
papers.abstract: Transcriptomics datasets generated using next-generation sequencing techniques such as single cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) and spatially-resolved transcriptomics (SRT) allow researchers to study patterns in gene expression across celltypes, temporal processes, and spatial organization at ever-higher resolutions and depths. scRNA-seq analyses produce gene expression profiles and celltype-specific gene sets that require annotation to provide biological meaning, a process that has traditionally relied on the manual interpretations of clinical scientists. Similarly, SRT experiments typically re
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: genesetGPT is a new tool that uses large language models (LLMs) to automatically generate plain-language summaries of gene sets from transcriptomics data, such as those from single-cell and spatial experiments. This reduces the need for manual annotation by clinical scientists, making biological interpretation faster and more accessible.

papers.title: BioPathfinder: Evidence-guided multi-agent platform enables hypothesis discovery for CAR-T engineering.
papers.abstract: Clinical studies of chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T therapy generate diverse molecular and clinical evidence that remains fragmented across publications, public repositories and patient-derived datasets, limiting systematic therapeutic discovery. Here we present BioPathfinder, an evidence-guided multi-agent workflow for closed-loop biomedical discovery. BioPathfinder constructs a provenance-aware knowledge resource linking publications with patient single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) datasets and clinical metadata, and uses role-specialized large language model agents to generate, review
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: BioPathfinder is a new multi-agent platform that integrates fragmented CAR-T therapy evidence from publications, patient single-cell RNA-seq data, and clinical metadata into a provenance-aware knowledge resource. It uses role-specialized LLM agents to generate and review hypotheses, enabling systematic therapeutic discovery for CAR-T engineering.

papers.title: Sequence determinants of pathogenicity in glucose-6-phosphatase linked to glycogen storage disease type 1a.
papers.abstract: Glycogen storage disease type 1a (GSD1a) is an autosomal recessive Mendelian disorder that can be caused by missense variants in glucose-6-phosphatase catalytic subunit 1 (G6PC1). Although hundreds of missense variants have been identified, the vast majority are of unknown clinical significance, and the molecular mechanism(s) of bona fide pathogenic variants are ill-defined. We combine bioinformatic data and clinical associations with the protein language model AlphaMissense to guide mechanistic exploration of 78 missense variants at 55 residue positions using robust biochemical and biophysica
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study investigates how missense variants in the G6PC1 gene cause glycogen storage disease type 1a by combining bioinformatic predictions (including AlphaMissense) with biochemical and biophysical experiments on 78 variants. The findings reveal sequence determinants of pathogenicity and provide mechanistic insights into how these variants disrupt enzyme function, which may improve variant classification for clinical diagnosis.

papers.title: Early Detection Methods for Autism Spectrum Disorder: From Clinical Screening to Multimodal AI.
papers.abstract: Early detection of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) in young children is essential for timely referral, developmental monitoring, and access to early intervention. However, conventional screening and diagnostic pathways often depend on parent-report instruments, episodic clinical observation, and specialist-administered assessments, which may delay identification during the first years of life. This scoping review maps the methodological landscape of early ASD detection from traditional clinical screening to multimodal artificial intelligence (AI). A structured literature search was conducted ac
papers.summary: This scoping review maps the methodological landscape of early autism spectrum disorder (ASD) detection, covering traditional clinical screening tools and emerging multimodal artificial intelligence approaches. It highlights the limitations of current parent-report and specialist-based methods and discusses how AI could improve early identification, though the review is descriptive rather than presenting new empirical findings.

papers.title: Dynamic Quality Prediction and Intelligent Classification of Litopenaeus vannamei in Cold Chain Based on Tad-Transformer.
papers.abstract: Temperature fluctuations in cold chain logistics accelerate protein degradation, lipid oxidation, and color deterioration of Litopenaeus vannamei, reducing product value and compromising food safety. To address this issue, this paper proposes a dynamic quality prediction method based on the Tad-Transformer neural network. First, storage experiments were conducted under six cold chain temperature conditions to collect multi-dimensional physicochemical and texture data. Core quality indicators were selected through temperature sensitivity analysis, and a time-series dataset was constructed. Seco
papers.summary: This paper presents a Tad-Transformer neural network model to dynamically predict the quality of Litopenaeus vannamei (whiteleg shrimp) during cold chain logistics, using multi-dimensional physicochemical and texture data collected under various temperature conditions. The model enables intelligent classification of shrimp quality, addressing quality deterioration caused by temperature fluctuations.

papers.title: Machine learning of sunitinib resistance genes reveals that SP5 regulates angiogenesis and sunitinib resistance in RCC via the VEGFA/AKT axis.
papers.abstract: Sunitinib resistance remains a major clinical challenge in renal cell carcinoma, and the underlying molecular mechanisms are incompletely understood. SP5, a member of the specificity protein transcription factor family, has been implicated in tumor progression, but its role in sunitinib resistance and angiogenesis in RCC is unclear.
papers.summary: This study uses machine learning to identify genes associated with sunitinib resistance in renal cell carcinoma (RCC), revealing that the transcription factor SP5 promotes angiogenesis and resistance to sunitinib through the VEGFA/AKT signaling axis. The findings suggest SP5 as a potential therapeutic target to overcome sunitinib resistance in RCC.

papers.title: Biallelic loss of RB1 in hepatocellular carcinoma as synthetic lethal target for artificial intelligence-guided therapy.
papers.abstract: The retinoblastoma (RB1) gene is a critical tumor suppressor that regulates cell cycle progression and genomic stability. Although RB1 alterations have been reported in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), the biological and clinical consequences of biallelic RB1 inactivation (RB1-Bi) remain poorly defined. We performed a comprehensive allele-specific genomic analysis of HCC patients from the TCGA-LIHC (n = 355) and in-house AMC (n = 206) cohorts, collectively comprising the AMC-TCGA discovery cohort. In this combined cohort, RB1-Bi was identified in 14.6% of tumors, was enriched in poorly differen
papers.summary: This study characterizes biallelic inactivation of the RB1 tumor suppressor in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), finding it in 14.6% of tumors and associated with poor differentiation. The authors propose RB1-Bi as a synthetic lethal target and use artificial intelligence to guide therapy, suggesting a potential precision oncology approach for this aggressive HCC subtype.

papers.title: Machine learning-derived serum carbon dioxide trajectories in predicting prognosis of patients with acute aortic dissection.
papers.abstract: JOURNAL/mgres/04.03/01612956-990000000-00114/figure1/v/2026-08-19T154102Z/r/image-tiff Venous partial pressure of carbon dioxide (PvCO2) indicates postoperative adverse outcomes in patients with acute aortic dissection, and its trajectories over time affecting postoperative adverse outcomes remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate the relationship between PvCO2 trajectories and postoperative adverse outcomes, as well as clinical application through group-based trajectory modeling and machine-learning algorithms. This retrospective cohort study analyzed data from 642 patients with acute
papers.summary: This study used machine learning and group-based trajectory modeling to identify distinct serum carbon dioxide (PvCO2) trajectories in patients with acute aortic dissection, finding that certain trajectory patterns are associated with worse postoperative outcomes. The approach demonstrates the potential of trajectory-based machine learning for prognostic prediction in this clinical setting.

papers.title: The Continuity Trap in Data Science Health Research.
papers.abstract: Secondary use is now the ordinary condition of data science health research rather than an exception to it. Electronic health records collected for clinical care become prediction tools and inputs for generative AI; imaging archives become foundation-model corpora; genomic datasets become resources for polygenic risk scores; and legacy biospecimens become renewable, indefinitely distributable cell lines. Governance has responded by emphasizing verifiable instruments such as provenance logs, repository approvals, broad-consent forms, data-use agreements, model cards, records of processing, and
papers.summary: This paper argues that secondary use of health data is now the norm in data science research, and that current governance frameworks—which rely on static, verifiable instruments like consent forms and data-use agreements—are ill-equipped to handle the continuous, evolving nature of data reuse. The authors propose that this 'continuity trap' requires a shift in governance thinking to address the dynamic lifecycle of health data.

papers.title: AI-Guided Computational Design of Synthetic Microbiota for Next-Generation Immunomodulatory Applications.
papers.abstract: The growing recognition of the human microbiome as a key regulator of immune homeostasis has accelerated the application of computational intelligence for microbiome-driven disease understanding and therapeutic design. However, existing microbiome studies largely rely on classical machine learning or shallow deep learning models that fail to capture higher-order microbial interactions, multimodal functional dependencies, and immune feasibility constraints simultaneously. Moreover, most approaches lack biological constraint enforcement, leading to predictions that may be statistically accurate
papers.summary: This review discusses the use of AI-guided computational design to create synthetic microbiota for immunomodulatory therapies, highlighting limitations of current machine learning models in capturing complex microbial interactions and enforcing biological constraints. It emphasizes the need for advanced AI approaches that integrate higher-order interactions and immune feasibility to improve therapeutic design.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Post-translational Modification Site Prediction: Progress and Future Perspectives.
papers.abstract: Post-translational modifications (PTMs) are pivotal in modulating protein function and cellular processes. However, experimental identification of PTM sites remains costly and labor-intensive. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have enabled accurate and scalable in silico PTM site prediction from large-scale proteomic data. In this review, we provide a comprehensive and up-to-date overview of AI-driven PTM site prediction across more than ten PTM classes, covering single-PTM site prediction, multiple-PTM site prediction, inter-site crosstalk prediction, and functional prediction o
papers.summary: This review provides a comprehensive overview of AI-driven methods for predicting post-translational modification (PTM) sites, covering more than ten PTM classes and various prediction tasks including single-PTM, multiple-PTM, inter-site crosstalk, and functional prediction. It highlights recent advances in using artificial intelligence to enable accurate and scalable in silico prediction from large-scale proteomic data, addressing the high cost and labor intensity of experimental identification.

papers.title: Integration of single-cell transcriptomics and genomic mutation analysis identifies an immunotherapy-resistant tumor subcluster and validates ARNTL2 as a malignant driver in lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Immunotherapy resistance in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remains a critical clinical challenge, and the mechanisms underlying resistance-associated intratumoral heterogeneity are poorly characterized.
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell transcriptomics with genomic mutation analysis in lung adenocarcinoma to identify a tumor subcluster associated with immunotherapy resistance, and validates ARNTL2 as a key malignant driver in this context. The findings provide new insights into resistance mechanisms and highlight a potential therapeutic target.

papers.title: Multi-Omics Integration Identifies a CDH3-Associated Malignant Epithelial State and Immunosuppressive Niche to Predict Prognosis in Thymic Epithelial Tumors.
papers.abstract: Thymic epithelial tumors (TETs) are rare and heterogeneous malignancies whose aggressive epithelial states and microenvironmental organization remain poorly defined. Here, we integrated single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, multiplex immunofluorescence, bulk transcriptomics, functional assays, xenograft validation, and computational pathology to characterize malignant epithelial heterogeneity in TETs. We identified a CDH3-associated malignant epithelial state located at the origin of malignant-state trajectories and enriched for stem-like and EMT-related features. Spatial transc
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and other approaches to characterize malignant epithelial heterogeneity in thymic epithelial tumors (TETs). The authors identify a CDH3-associated malignant epithelial state with stem-like and EMT features that predicts prognosis and is linked to an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment.

papers.title: Structure-aware deep learning enhances m6A prediction and reveals cell type-associated RNA structural signatures.
papers.abstract: N6-methyladenosine (m6A), the most abundant mRNA modification in eukaryotes, plays essential roles in gene regulation and disease pathogenesis. Computational prediction of m6A sites offers a scalable alternative to costly experimental approaches, yet current methods rely predominantly on linear sequence features. This overlooks potentially informative RNA structural context, which is associated with local methylation patterns and may provide complementary predictive information beyond linear sequence motifs. To incorporate this complementary information, we propose SMART-m6A (Sequence-structur
papers.summary: This paper introduces SMART-m6A, a deep learning method that incorporates RNA structural information alongside sequence data to improve prediction of m6A modification sites. The approach reveals cell type-associated RNA structural signatures, demonstrating that structural context provides complementary predictive information beyond linear sequence motifs.

papers.title: Computationally Evidence-Grounded Sequence-First Design of Peptide Binders.
papers.abstract: Peptide binders provide a versatile modality for modulating protein targets that are poorly addressed by small molecules, but their discovery is constrained by sample-intensive screening or reliance on structural templates. Sequence-first generation offers a scalable alternative for targets lacking stable or representative structures, yet existing approaches often sacrifice target-specific control for diversity and are further limited by the imperfect transfer of protein language-model priors to short peptides. Here, we report BOND-PEP, an evidence-grounded framework for sequence-only peptide
papers.summary: The paper introduces BOND-PEP, a computational framework for designing peptide binders using only sequence information, without requiring structural templates. It addresses limitations of existing sequence-first methods by improving target-specific control and adapting protein language models to short peptides, offering a scalable alternative for targets lacking stable structures.

papers.title: Peptide language pragmatic analysis and two-stage hierarchical learning framework for therapeutic peptide prediction.
papers.abstract: Therapeutic peptides exert pivotal effects in diverse biological processes, and have attracted significant interest in the field of biomedicine in recent years. However, most existing methods often fail to adequately capture the intricate interactions among amino acid residues and the contextual dependencies within peptide sequences, which hampers the extraction of deep semantic representations and ultimately restricts predictive performance. Moreover, the task of multi-functional therapeutic peptide prediction is inherently constrained by the challenge of imbalanced multi-label classification
papers.summary: This paper presents a new computational framework that uses a peptide language model and a two-stage hierarchical learning approach to improve prediction of therapeutic peptide functions. It addresses limitations of existing methods by better capturing amino acid interactions and handling imbalanced multi-label classification, leading to more accurate predictions.

papers.title: Exploring dual-use risks of large language models for new psychoactive substances: a severity-based vulnerability analysis.
papers.abstract: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have profoundly transformed scientific research in chemistry, enabling literature mining, the prediction of physicochemical and biological properties, and even the generation of novel molecular structures. However, such tools also raise concerns regarding malicious use, particularly in the context of the clandestine synthesis of new psychoactive substances (NPSs). In this study, we evaluate simulated scenarios of interaction with LLM-based chatbots to explore potential vulnerabilities in the provision of information that could facilitate illicit
papers.journal: The International journal on drug policy
papers.summary: This study evaluates how large language models (LLMs) could be misused to facilitate the clandestine synthesis of new psychoactive substances (NPSs), identifying vulnerabilities in the information they provide. The authors propose a severity-based vulnerability analysis to assess and mitigate dual-use risks, highlighting the need for safeguards in chemistry-focused AI tools.

papers.title: Generalizable cancer detection from ultra-low-pass WGS via deep contextual modeling of cfDNA sequences.
papers.abstract: Ultra-low-pass whole-genome sequencing (ULP-WGS) of cell-free DNA (cfDNA) offers a cost-efficient strategy for cancer detection, but its clinical application is limited by extreme data sparsity and poor model generalization. We developed Fragmentia-AI™ WGS, a mutation-calling-independent framework that uses a transformer-based multiple-instance learning architecture with sequential fine-tuning across tumor fraction (TF) strata to extract latent cancer-associated signals from ULP-WGS data. Model performance was evaluated in multiple independent cohorts, including a pan-cancer test set covering
papers.summary: This paper introduces Fragmentia-AI™ WGS, a transformer-based deep learning framework that detects cancer from ultra-low-pass whole-genome sequencing of cell-free DNA without relying on mutation calling. The model uses multiple-instance learning and sequential fine-tuning across tumor fraction strata to extract cancer-associated signals from sparse data, demonstrating improved generalization across multiple independent pan-cancer cohorts.

papers.title: Using the DNA language model, GROVER, to parse effects of sequence, chromatin and regulatory features on genome stability.
papers.abstract: Genome stability is shaped by DNA sequence and chromatin context, but their relative contributions to double-strand break (DSB) sensitivity remain unclear.
papers.summary: This paper applies GROVER, a DNA language model, to investigate how DNA sequence and chromatin features influence genome stability, specifically double-strand break (DSB) sensitivity. The study demonstrates that the model can parse the relative contributions of sequence and regulatory context, offering a new computational approach to understanding genomic instability.

papers.title: DeepPNI: a language- and graph-based model for mutation-driven protein-nucleic acid binding energetics.
papers.abstract: Protein-nucleic acid interactions (PNIs) are central to fundamental biological processes, and mutations can disrupt these interactions by altering local structural features and binding free energy. Here, we present DeepPNI, a deep learning regression model that integrates sequence- and structure-based features to estimate mutation-induced changes in binding free energy in protein-nucleic acid complexes. The model was developed using a comprehensive dataset of 1754 mutations spanning protein-DNA and protein-RNA complexes, representing one of the largest curated datasets for PNI binding free ene
papers.summary: DeepPNI is a new deep learning model that predicts how mutations change the binding strength of protein-nucleic acid interactions (like protein-DNA and protein-RNA). It combines sequence and structural information and was trained on a large curated dataset of 1,754 mutations, making it a valuable tool for understanding mutation effects in these key biological processes.

papers.title: DNAreader: accurate prediction of DNA-binding residues in structured and disordered proteins using transformers and contrastive learning.
papers.abstract: Accurate predictions of DNA-binding residues (DBRs) in protein sequences facilitate decoding molecular-level mechanisms underlying cellular functions that involve protein-DNA interactions. While dozens of these predictors have been released, they target either structured or intrinsically disordered regions (IDRs), and the latter were trained to predict less detailed DNA-binding IDRs rather than DBRs. Given this dichotomy, the structure-trained methods underperform on disordered proteins, and vice versa. Moreover, they suffer from high cross-prediction rates, incorrectly labeling many residues
papers.summary: DNAreader is a new deep learning tool that accurately predicts DNA-binding residues in both structured and disordered proteins, overcoming the limitations of existing predictors that specialize in only one type. It uses transformers and contrastive learning to reduce false positives and improve generalization across protein types.

papers.title: AI semantics for biomedical data integration.
papers.abstract: Researchers increasingly need to explore hypotheses that span multimodal data across different scales, organisms, and domains. In practice, this requires connecting knowledge across fragmented databases with incompatible APIs and heterogeneous annotation practices. Large language model (LLM) agents can automate this data integration process, but grounding LLM agent outputs in scientifically correct sources of truth remains a significant challenge. Here we describe our deployment of a novel AI semantics workflow using LLM agents to enable scalable data integration, grounded in biological knowle
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint describes a novel AI semantics workflow that uses large language model (LLM) agents to automate the integration of multimodal biomedical data across fragmented databases with incompatible APIs and heterogeneous annotations. The workflow grounds LLM agent outputs in biological knowledge to ensure scientific correctness, addressing a key challenge in scalable data integration.

papers.title: PlantCAD2: A DNA foundation model for interpreting genomes across flowering plants.
papers.abstract: Flowering plants (angiosperms) exhibit extraordinary species diversity, ∼200-fold variation in genome size, and relatively compact coding regions, presenting both a unique challenge and opportunity for DNA language models. Here, we introduce PlantCAD2, an extended-context, plant-specific DNA language model with single-nucleotide resolution, pre-trained on 65 angiosperm genomes, together with a series of public benchmarks for evaluation. Comprehensive zero-shot testing shows that PlantCAD2 (676 million parameters) efficiently captures evolutionary conservation, surpassing the 7-billion-paramete
papers.summary: PlantCAD2 is a new DNA foundation model pre-trained on 65 flowering plant genomes that captures evolutionary conservation with single-nucleotide resolution, outperforming much larger models in zero-shot tests. It provides a resource for interpreting plant genomes and includes public benchmarks for evaluation.

papers.title: Tau reduction counteracts transcriptomic and behavioral abnormalities in an Alzheimer amyloid model.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) causes amyloid formation, neuritic dystrophy, gliosis, synapse loss, behavioral abnormalities, and weight loss. 5xFAD transgenic mice simulate these alterations. To further investigate overall tau reduction as a therapeutic strategy for AD-related abnormalities, we compared 5xFAD mice carrying 2, 1, or 0 Mapt alleles encoding endogenous wildtype tau. Behavioral alterations in 5xFAD mice detected by a machine learning algorithm were prevented or minimized by tau reduction, although 5xFAD/ Mapt +/+ mice had no classical tau pathology. Reduction of nonfibrillar tau also p
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint shows that reducing endogenous tau levels in 5xFAD Alzheimer's model mice prevents or minimizes behavioral abnormalities and transcriptomic changes, even though the mice lack classical tau pathology. The findings suggest that nonfibrillar tau plays a key role in driving disease-related dysfunction, supporting tau reduction as a potential therapeutic strategy.

papers.title: HaloMPNN: retraining ProteinMPNN on halophilic proteomes for salt-tolerant enzyme design.
papers.abstract: Machine learning-guided protein sequence redesign is now routinely used to optimize multiple properties relevant for protein engineering, most prominently thermostability and recombinant expression levels. Salt tolerance is a valuable property for "blue-biotechnology"- enabled biomanufacturing, yet no generative computational method exists to redesign proteins for increased salt tolerance. We hypothesized that a training dataset heavily biased toward salt-adapted proteomes would yield a model capable of designing proteins with halophilic properties. To test this, we retrained the sequence rede
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors retrained ProteinMPNN on halophilic proteomes to create HaloMPNN, a generative model for designing salt-tolerant enzymes. This is the first computational method specifically for increasing protein salt tolerance, addressing a gap in protein engineering for blue biotechnology.

papers.title: Fine-grained structural classification of biosynthetic gene cluster-encoded products.
papers.abstract: Biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) are responsible the biosynthesis of many natural products, including a multitude of effective therapeutics and their precursors. Advances in genomic data collection as well as computational techniques have made it possible to identify BGCs at scale. However, accurately determining the types of BGC-encoded products from genomic content remains elusive.
papers.summary: This paper presents a computational method for fine-grained structural classification of products encoded by biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs), addressing the challenge of accurately determining product types from genomic data. The approach improves upon existing tools by enabling more detailed classification, which could aid in natural product discovery and drug development.

papers.title: Integrated Analysis of SNPs and Structural Variations via High-depth Whole-genome Sequencing Reveals the Genetic Architecture and Optimizes Genomic Prediction in Chickens.
papers.abstract: The characterization of genetic architecture and the optimization of genomic prediction are pivotal for the genetic improvement of complex traits in poultry. In this study, we investigated the genetic basis of 15 growth and carcass traits in an F2 chicken population (n = 877) using high-depth whole-genome sequencing with an average coverage of 31.2 × . By implementing an ensemble strategy involving four independent callers, we identified 35,924 high-confidence structural variations (SVs), with deletions being the most prevalent type. Combining SNPs and SVs enhanced genomic heritability for 14
papers.summary: This study used high-depth whole-genome sequencing to identify structural variants (SVs) in an F2 chicken population and combined them with SNPs to analyze the genetic architecture of growth and carcass traits. Integrating SVs with SNPs improved genomic heritability estimates and genomic prediction accuracy for these traits, highlighting the value of including SVs in genetic improvement programs.

papers.title: Benchmarking Deep Learning Predictions of Mutation-Induced Fold Switching.
papers.abstract: Many proteins are known to adopt multiple distinct folded states which are often associated with key functional behavior. A predictive understanding of the properties of such fold-switching or metamorphic proteins can provide insights into protein dynamics and energetics, and enable the design of complex protein functions and molecular machines. Recently developed deep learning modeling tools, including AlphaFold, have led to dramatic increases in accuracy for prediction of protein structures from sequence, but their performance for prediction of point mutant effects or fold switching is uncle
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint benchmarks deep learning protein structure prediction tools, including AlphaFold, for their ability to predict mutation-induced fold switching in metamorphic proteins. The study finds that current deep learning methods have limited accuracy for this challenging task, highlighting gaps in predicting conformational changes from sequence.

papers.title: SPINDLE: Unlocking protein dynamics from single-field NMR relaxation data using a deep learning ensemble.
papers.abstract: A protein's function is derived from its three-dimensional structure and the motions of the atoms about that structure. The detailed characterization of both macromolecular structure and dynamics provides an opportunity for understanding enzyme catalysis, ligand binding, and allostery, along with providing insights into how the function changes upon mutation or post-translational modification. Among the various methods for characterizing biomolecular motions, nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spin relaxation methods are a standard for determining nanosecond global tumbling times along with the
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: SPINDLE is a deep learning ensemble that predicts protein dynamics from single-field NMR relaxation data, overcoming the need for multiple magnetic field strengths. It enables detailed characterization of nanosecond timescale motions, which is crucial for understanding enzyme catalysis, ligand binding, and allostery.

papers.title: scKanFormer: A Transformer-KAN framework with biologically informed attention for cell type annotation in large-scale scRNA-seq data.
papers.abstract: A key challenge in single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data analysis is accurately and efficiently identifying the cell type of each cell. Cell type annotation for scRNA-seq data not only needs to overcome batch effects caused by various factors but also requires effective handling of large-scale scRNA-seq datasets. Although deep learning has achieved remarkable progress in cell type annotation tasks, it still exhibits limitations in interpretability and robustness against batch effects. To tackle these issues, we propose a supervised framework based on the Transformer architecture, named s
papers.summary: The paper introduces scKanFormer, a Transformer-based framework enhanced with Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KAN) and biologically informed attention for cell type annotation in large-scale scRNA-seq data. It addresses limitations in interpretability and robustness against batch effects, offering a more reliable and efficient annotation method.

papers.title: Deep learning for optoacoustic imaging of reversibly switchable proteins: training and performance testing using simulated multispectral optoacoustic tomography images.
papers.abstract: Reversibly switchable optoacoustic proteins (rsOAPs) are a promising candidate for sensitive and quantitative optoacoustic (OA) imaging of genetically modified cell populations, such as chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cells used in cancer immunotherapy. Although detection of rsOAPs has been demonstrated using classical machine learning approaches, there is still a need for higher detection sensitivity and more accurate quantification.
papers.summary: This paper presents a deep learning approach for detecting and quantifying reversibly switchable optoacoustic proteins (rsOAPs) in multispectral optoacoustic tomography images, using simulated data for training and testing. The method aims to improve sensitivity and accuracy over classical machine learning, with potential applications in imaging CAR T-cells for cancer immunotherapy.

papers.title: SiaRNA: a siamese neural network with bidirectional cross-attention for pairwise siRNA-mRNA efficacy prediction.
papers.abstract: Small interfering RNA (siRNA) therapeutics have extraordinary potential for targeted gene silencing. They mediate post-transcriptional gene regulation by binding to complementary messenger RNA (mRNA) sequences and degrading them, thereby preventing the production of unwanted proteins. Recent machine learning and deep learning frameworks for predicting siRNA efficacy have only achieved moderate success as these models solely rely either on handcrafted features or on sequential relations and therefore cannot capture the full complexity of siRNA-mRNA interactions.
papers.summary: This paper introduces SiaRNA, a siamese neural network with bidirectional cross-attention that predicts siRNA-mRNA efficacy by jointly modeling both sequences. It addresses limitations of prior models that relied only on handcrafted features or single-sequence relations, potentially improving the accuracy of siRNA therapeutic design.

papers.title: Triglyceride-glucose index and hyperhomocysteinemia within a cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic biomarker network: insights from interpretable machine learning and epidemiological modeling.
papers.abstract: Although the triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index is an established surrogate marker of insulin resistance and metabolic burden, its relationship with hyperhomocysteinemia (HHcy) within the cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) framework remains insufficiently understood. This study aimed to investigate the association between TyG and HHcy and to prioritize CKM-related biomarkers using interpretable machine learning and epidemiological modeling.
papers.summary: This study investigates the relationship between the triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index and hyperhomocysteinemia (HHcy) within the context of cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome, using interpretable machine learning and epidemiological modeling. The findings reveal a significant association between TyG and HHcy and identify key CKM-related biomarkers, providing new insights into the interconnected metabolic pathways underlying CKM syndrome.

papers.title: Admission laboratory parameters for early risk stratification after aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage: a machine learning analysis of real-world data.
papers.abstract: Aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH) is associated with substantial morbidity and mortality. Early risk stratification is essential for treatment planning and prognostication, yet neurological assessment may be limited in sedated or critically ill patients. Routine admission laboratory parameters may provide additional prognostic information and improve machine learning (ML)-based outcome prediction.
papers.summary: This study uses machine learning on real-world data to evaluate whether routine admission laboratory parameters can improve early risk stratification after aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage. The findings suggest that these readily available lab values add prognostic value, potentially aiding outcome prediction in patients where neurological assessment is limited.

papers.title: A machine learning framework for predictive interpretation of variants of uncertain significance in hereditary cancer.
papers.abstract: Variant interpretation remains a major bottleneck in clinical genomics, with variants of uncertain significance (VUS) representing a critical unresolved challenge due to insufficient evidence for definitive classification. Existing in silico tools exhibit variable and often inconsistent performance complicating clinical decision-making, particularly in the context of hereditary cancer genomics.
papers.summary: This paper presents a machine learning framework designed to improve the predictive interpretation of variants of uncertain significance (VUS) in hereditary cancer genes. The framework aims to address the inconsistency of existing in silico tools by providing more reliable classifications to aid clinical decision-making.

papers.title: Boundary-aware and uncertainty-guided deep learning for multimodal magnetic resonance imaging segmentation of stroke lesions.
papers.abstract: Acute ischemic stroke is a major cerebrovascular disease, and accurate lesion segmentation is important for quantitative image analysis and subsequent clinical assessment. Multimodal magnetic resonance imaging, including diffusion-weighted imaging, apparent diffusion coefficient maps, and fluid-attenuated inversion recovery, provides complementary information for lesion delineation. However, lesion appearance may vary across sequences, and blurred boundaries or small scattered lesions can make multimodal feature fusion unstable.
papers.summary: This paper presents a deep learning method for segmenting acute ischemic stroke lesions in multimodal MRI, addressing challenges like blurred boundaries and small lesions. The approach integrates boundary-aware and uncertainty-guided modules to improve segmentation accuracy and stability across diffusion-weighted imaging, apparent diffusion coefficient maps, and fluid-attenuated inversion recovery sequences.

papers.title: A tissue microenvironment analogous to certain tumor microenvironments facilitates HIV persistence.
papers.abstract: The HIV reservoir that establishes early upon infection and persists in tissues remains the primary barrier to a functional cure. While progress has been made to study the reservoir in blood compartments and specific cell types, knowledge gaps remain on the tissue microenvironment that facilitates persistence. The development of a novel immunoPET/CT-guided spatial transcriptomics pipeline has enabled the localization of foci of viral infection in tissues, rare events that are challenging to sample. Prior studies leveraging the pipeline have characterized the viral microenvironment (VME) gene s
papers.summary: This paper discusses how certain tissue microenvironments, similar to those found in tumors, help HIV persist in the body despite antiretroviral therapy. The authors use a novel immunoPET/CT-guided spatial transcriptomics approach to locate and characterize rare viral reservoirs in tissues, revealing gene expression patterns that support HIV persistence. This work highlights the importance of studying tissue-level microenvironments to develop strategies for an HIV cure.

papers.title: Plasmid-resolved genomics and machine learning-assisted profiling reveal Enterobacter soli as an overlooked host of a bla NDM-1-bearing IncX3 plasmid.
papers.abstract: Plasmid-mediated carbapenem resistance is a major public health concern, yet the role of under-characterized Enterobacter species in carrying clinically important resistance plasmids remains insufficiently defined. In particular, plasmid-resolved genomic information on bla NDM-1-positive Enterobacter soli is scarce, and it remains unclear whether clinical E. soli can harbor conserved bla NDM-1-bearing IncX3 plasmids related to those circulating among other Enterobacterales hosts.
papers.summary: This study uses plasmid-resolved genomics and machine learning to characterize Enterobacter soli as a previously overlooked carrier of a bla NDM-1-bearing IncX3 plasmid, which is clinically important for carbapenem resistance. The findings reveal that clinical E. soli can harbor conserved resistance plasmids related to those in other Enterobacterales, highlighting its potential role in spreading antibiotic resistance.

papers.title: TPT: a compact CNN-transformer encoder for efficient microbial small protein modeling.
papers.abstract: Microbial small proteins, encoded by small open reading frames (smORFs), play essential roles in antimicrobial activity, metabolic regulation, and signaling pathways. However, their short length and rapid evolutionary rate present significant challenges for computational modeling.
papers.summary: This paper introduces TPT, a compact CNN-transformer hybrid encoder designed to improve computational modeling of microbial small proteins, which are difficult to analyze due to their short length and rapid evolution. The model efficiently captures both local and global sequence features, offering a new tool for studying these functionally important proteins.

papers.title: Microstructure-informed stage characterization of wheat endosperm refinement during shear comminution.
papers.abstract: Structural evolution of wheat endosperm particles during comminution can markedly influence flour processing and digestibility. While previous studies have mainly focused on differences among grinding endpoints, stage-dependent refinement under shear-dominant conditions remains unclear. This study characterized the structural and functional evolution of wheat endosperm particles during shear-dominant comminution. Coarse wheat endosperm particles were collected after predefined shear durations during shear-dominant comminution and examined using scanning electron microscopy and confocal laser s
papers.summary: This study characterizes how wheat endosperm particles structurally evolve during shear-dominant comminution, revealing stage-dependent refinement patterns that influence flour processing and digestibility. Using microscopy techniques, the authors identify distinct structural changes at different grinding stages, providing insights beyond endpoint comparisons.

papers.title: Ferroptosis-Related Diagnostic Biomarkers in Diabetic Kidney Disease: A Multi-Omics and Multi-Cohort Study.
papers.abstract: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is one of the primary factors leading to end-stage renal disease. Ferroptosis, as a mechanism-related form of programmed cell death, has garnered increasing attention in DKD research. This study aimed to identify and validate ferroptosis-related diagnostic biomarkers for DKD.
papers.summary: This study identifies and validates ferroptosis-related diagnostic biomarkers for diabetic kidney disease (DKD) using multi-omics and multi-cohort analyses. The findings provide potential biomarkers that could aid in early diagnosis and understanding of DKD pathogenesis.

papers.title: Multimodal AI in high-grade serous ovarian cancer: integrated prediction and clinical decision-making.
papers.abstract: Ovarian cancer remains the most lethal gynecologic malignancy, with high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma (HGSOC) accounting for the majority of deaths. It is typically diagnosed at an advanced stage, characterized by extensive peritoneal dissemination and high rates of recurrence, which contribute to persistently poor survival despite advances in cytoreductive surgery, platinum-based chemotherapy, and targeted therapies such as PARP inhibitors. Clinical outcomes are highly variable, reflecting substantial inter- and intratumoral heterogeneity at the genomic, cellular, and microenvironmental lev
papers.summary: This review discusses the potential of multimodal AI approaches that integrate genomic, cellular, and microenvironmental data to improve prediction and clinical decision-making in high-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC). It highlights how such integrated models could address the heterogeneity of the disease and ultimately improve patient outcomes.

papers.title: UNKAI: A Protein Functional Identity Prediction Model Based on ESM-C Latent Representations and the Attention Mechanism.
papers.abstract: The rapid advancement of genome sequencing technologies has led to the accumulation of a vast number of protein sequences in public databases. However, a substantial proportion of these proteins remain functionally uncharacterized. Concurrently, the expansion of protein sequence data has enabled the development of protein language models (pLMs). By distilling billions of years of evolutionary history into a latent representational space, these models have acquired an unprecedented capacity to predict both the tertiary structures and functions of proteins. In this study, we developed a deep lea
papers.summary: The paper introduces UNKAI, a deep learning model that predicts protein functional identity using ESM-C latent representations and an attention mechanism. It addresses the challenge of functionally uncharacterized proteins by leveraging protein language models to improve annotation accuracy.

papers.title: Clinical risk factors and machine learning for venous thromboembolism in lung cancer: an exploratory single-center study.
papers.abstract: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) represents a common and severe comorbidity in lung cancer patients. This study aimed to characterize the clinical features and independent risk factors associated with VTE in these individuals, and to evaluate the complementary utility of machine learning approaches in enhancing VTE risk stratification.
papers.summary: This exploratory single-center study identifies clinical risk factors for venous thromboembolism (VTE) in lung cancer patients and evaluates machine learning models for VTE risk stratification. The findings suggest that machine learning can complement traditional risk assessment, potentially improving prediction of this serious comorbidity.

papers.title: A biologically structured hierarchical vision transformer-CNN framework for robust tomato leaf disease classification.
papers.abstract: Precise and reliable diagnosis of leaf diseases in tomato is essential for enhancing crop cultivation and minimizing agricultural losses. While deep learning models have performed well on benchmark datasets, the majority of present techniques rely on flat multi-class classification, which predicts all disease categories simultaneously. Such formulations promotes inter-class confusion, particularly when biologically different diseases with similar visual symptoms are learned within a same model. To overcome this constraint, we propose a biologically structured hierarchical deep learning framewo
papers.summary: This paper proposes a hierarchical deep learning framework that combines vision transformers and CNNs to classify tomato leaf diseases, addressing the issue of inter-class confusion in flat multi-class classification by structuring the model according to biological disease relationships. The approach aims to improve diagnostic accuracy for visually similar diseases, potentially reducing agricultural losses.

papers.title: Generative AI-augmented transcriptomic and microbiome analysis across inflammatory and fibrotic disease states in Crohn's disease.
papers.abstract: Intestinal fibrosis is a major complication of Crohn's disease (CD), a subtype of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) driven by chronic inflammation and resulting in irreversible structural damage requiring surgery. However, the molecular differences between inflammatory and fibrotic CD remain poorly defined.
papers.summary: This study uses generative AI to analyze transcriptomic and microbiome data from Crohn's disease patients, aiming to distinguish between inflammatory and fibrotic disease states. The approach identifies molecular signatures that differentiate these conditions, potentially improving diagnosis and treatment targeting for intestinal fibrosis.

papers.title: Representations of facial features and surface quality in monkey area TE compared to neural network models.
papers.abstract: The shape and spacing of facial features are essential for the perception of emotional expressions and the identification of individuals. The surface quality of faces, such as skin texture, eye twinkle, and hair gloss, is valuable for estimating health status. A previous fMRI study in monkeys revealed that regions selective for faces overlapped regions selective for object gloss in the central inferior temporal (IT) cortex, suggesting that the surface quality of faces is processed in area TE. However, the representation of facial surface quality has not been directly examined in this area. To
papers.summary: This study investigates how monkey area TE represents facial features and surface quality, comparing these representations to neural network models. The findings reveal that area TE encodes both facial shape/spacing and surface quality, with neural network models showing partial alignment with biological representations.

papers.title: A generative AI multi-agent framework with integrated XAI governance for cancer diagnostics: from multi-omics interpretation to lifestyle risk stratification.
papers.abstract: Cancer diagnostics is being reshaped by rapid advances in artificial intelligence, yet a persistent gap separates computational performance from clinical trust. Systematic reviews confirm that 83% of XAI studies in oncology excluded clinicians from development or evaluation, 87% lacked rigorous assessment of XAI explanations, and no universally accepted quality metrics for XAI outputs currently exist. Concurrently, generative AI (GenAI) is entering oncology at an unprecedented pace, yet it operates largely without formal interpretability governance.
papers.summary: This paper proposes a generative AI multi-agent framework for cancer diagnostics that integrates explainable AI (XAI) governance to bridge the gap between computational performance and clinical trust. It addresses the lack of clinician involvement and rigorous evaluation in current XAI studies by incorporating governance mechanisms for interpretability, and extends the framework to include lifestyle risk stratification alongside multi-omics interpretation.

papers.title: DFN-kcr: a dual-branch deep learning model with attention-guided fusion for predicting lysine crotonylation sites in human non-histone proteins.
papers.abstract: Lysine crotonylation (Kcr) is extensively present in human non-histone proteins and plays a critical regulatory role in essential biological processes, including cell signaling and metabolic regulation. However, conventional wet-lab approaches for Kcr site identification are costly, time-consuming, and ill-suited for large-scale profiling. Although computational prediction methods have garnered increasing attention in recent years, there remains a notable lack of efficient and specialized tools tailored specifically for Kcr site prediction in human non-histone proteins.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This paper introduces DFN-kcr, a dual-branch deep learning model with attention-guided fusion for predicting lysine crotonylation (Kcr) sites in human non-histone proteins. The model addresses the lack of specialized computational tools for this task, offering a more efficient alternative to costly and time-consuming wet-lab experiments.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence in peptide cancer vaccine design: from neoantigen discovery to immunogenicity prediction.
papers.abstract: Peptide-based cancer vaccines represent a promising immunotherapeutic strategy aimed at inducing tumor-specific immune responses through the targeting of tumor-associated antigens and neoantigens. Recent advances in next-generation sequencing and immunogenomics have accelerated the identification of candidate neoantigens; however, the development of effective peptide vaccines remains limited by challenges related to antigen selection, HLA polymorphism, antigen processing, and variability in immunogenicity. Artificial intelligence (AI), including machine learning and deep learning approaches, h
papers.summary: This review discusses how artificial intelligence, including machine learning and deep learning, is being applied to improve peptide-based cancer vaccine design, from neoantigen discovery to immunogenicity prediction. It highlights how AI can address challenges such as antigen selection, HLA polymorphism, and variability in immunogenicity, offering a promising path toward more effective personalized cancer vaccines.

papers.title: Instability of LLM text embeddings for unsupervised dimension reduction of tabular data.
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) text embeddings have recently been used for supervised learning on tabular data by serializing each observation into text and then converting the text into a dense fixed-length vector. This strategy is appealing for biomedical tabular data, which are often mixed-type and contain missing values, because it produces a complete numeric representation even when some original entries are missing. However, its suitability for unsupervised tasks remains unclear. Here we evaluate the use of LLM-derived text embeddings for dimension reduction of tabular data, focusing on biol
papers.summary: This study evaluates whether LLM text embeddings, created by serializing tabular data into text, are suitable for unsupervised dimension reduction of biomedical data. The authors find that these embeddings are unstable for such tasks, suggesting caution in using them for unsupervised analysis.

papers.title: Clinical AI-assisted FXR prioritization and WADDAICA-guided design of a berberine-inspired analogue for MASH: integrated computational and experimental validation.
papers.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), lack effective targeted therapies despite increasing global prevalence. The farnesoid X receptor (FXR) is a key regulator of hepatic lipid metabolism, inflammation, and fibrosis, making it a promising therapeutic target. However, existing FXR modulators are associated with limited efficacy and adverse effects.
papers.summary: This study uses clinical AI-assisted prioritization of the FXR target and a computational method called WADDAICA to design a berberine-inspired analogue for MASH, followed by experimental validation. The work integrates computational design with wet-lab testing to propose a new potential therapeutic candidate for MASH.
